# M4 progress

Started 2026-10-24 at the user's request. Goal: complete the full [M4 plan](M4-meetings-enrichment-operations.md) and specification §19, preserving the deployed M3 service and existing working-tree changes. M4 is not accepted or deployed.

## Implementation order

1. Transcript extraction, types, segments, retrieval/citation locators, people filters and viewer.
2. Calendar extraction and complete-container reconciliation, recurrence/coverage queries and event viewer.
3. Protected calendar subscriptions, bounded source-download transport, durable polling, source controls and freshness.
4. Reclassification/enrichment, provider adapters, budgets and usage attribution.
5. Encrypted backup/verified restore/export, retention and release supply-chain controls.
6. Full deterministic regression, real-export and live-feed qualification, browser/deployment acceptance and evidence.

## Current changes

- Added bounded WebVTT/SubRip parsing in the extraction sandbox. Voice changes and overlapping cue times retain exact text offsets; malformed cues fail explicitly. Transcript output is revalidated at the daemon boundary.
- Added the transcript property schema and physical-format precedence; participant/start-time capture, persisted segment projection, speaker/time chunk locators, role-qualified search, citation metadata and transcript rendering are being verified.
- Fixed reclassification to derive effective properties without discarding the originally ingested fields.
- Existing M3 files and configuration remain untouched on the running deployment. No M4 production migration or deployment has been attempted.

Desktop/phone browser qualification passed at 1280 and 390 pixels using a real sandboxed extractor and synthetic data. An initial browser run exposed a timestamp link resolving against the application base instead of the document; the link and its behavioral check were corrected, rebuilt with zero warnings/errors, and reverified. The [checkpoint evidence](evidence/m4-transcripts-20261024/verification.json), [browser checks](evidence/m4-transcripts-20261024/browser.json), and desktop/mobile screenshots retain the scope and limitations. The isolated fixtures have been stopped.

The historical M2 recorded-provider evaluation explicitly uses the original note/article/file registry. Adding transcript metadata changes the model's system prompt, so these original recordings cannot establish M4 model quality. Fresh live-model transcript/calendar qualification remains required; the existing recordings and human annotations have not been rewritten.

Earlier attempts caught and corrected a nullable-reference warning, search-column indexing compatibility, null metadata serialization, and Unicode speaker matching. A restricted-sandbox test invocation could not open the test runner's local sockets and was rerun with local network access. Those attempts are not acceptance evidence.

The protected subscription foundation now passes **2,078 deterministic Debug tests**, with warnings treated as errors and a successful locked restore. [Foundation evidence](evidence/m4-subscription-foundation-20261024/verification.json) records the scope and test limitations. The complete bearer URL uses a dedicated Data Protection purpose. Durable registration preserves source/container identities, coalesces refresh requests, reclaims expired leases, invalidates old source generations on pause/resume, preserves accepted validators after failures, and records retry/freshness state.

The download transport separately requires an exact HTTPS origin in `sources.calendar_allowed_origins`. It rejects nonpublic addresses and canary destinations, pins the validated address, disables redirects/proxies/cookies, and bounds headers, bytes, expansion and request duration. Response tests use controlled handlers; the rebinding test uses the real socket handler and confirms that the forbidden loopback listener receives no connection. A local probe found that runtime decompressors can return complete-looking text from truncated envelopes; explicit gzip/deflate integrity checks and a completion-aware Brotli reader now reject those responses. The composition and YAML golden changes were reviewed.

The next subscription checkpoint connects the foundation to durable polling, independent local recurrence materialization, REST/CLI/browser controls and query freshness. Accepted immutable snapshots, validators and member publication now complete through one recoverable group. A pending accepted group finishes before pause or removal acknowledges the authority change; downloads not yet accepted fail their old generation fence. Unchanged responses avoid document revisions, rejected bytes are remembered, and paused sources can advance retained recurrence coverage without claiming a fresh remote check.

Source administration now supports registration, listing, refresh/force refresh, name/interval edits, pause/resume and removal with existing scope, session and recent-password checks. `brain sources add-calendar --name "Shared calendar"` uses a dedicated hidden prompt; `--url-stdin` is bounded and avoids putting the link in command arguments. Queries return source freshness even when no events match. The Sources and Library views show stale/failed/paused input separately from recurrence coverage.

Configured subscriptions now accept only `${NAME}` references in `sources.calendar_subscriptions`. The loader retains references and validates resolved links without serializing them. Before polling starts, a single registry transaction reconciles the declared entries; rejected links, conflicting ids or admission failures leave the batch unapplied. Restarts preserve source/container identity, protected settings and leases. Omitting an entry pauses it; explicit removal remains a tombstone. Declared name/interval/enabled state is reapplied at startup, while API-created sources remain independent. Reload validation rejects a changed resolved link even if its reference name is unchanged. Source settings remain restart-only, consistent with the current deployment policy. This checkpoint passed **2,127 deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Calendar containers now have a coordinated trash/restore/purge lifecycle. Trashing a container hides its available members, removes their occurrence coverage and fences pending network work. Restore preserves member identities and independent event deletions. A subscription stays paused until explicitly resumed after restore; that lifecycle pause also survives reconciliation of enabled configuration entries on restart. Purging an individual event retains its container's owned originals. Purging the container erases its members, current and historical owned snapshot files, linked payloads and search projections through the recoverable publication workflow.

Bounded cleanup now removes detached, never-accepted snapshot imports. It preserves active leases, pending accepted publications, accepted history and externally replaced files; an interrupted quarantine is replayable. Cleanup runs with the polling recovery loop. Accepted historical snapshots remain retained until container purge; this does not implement general retention.

Calendar source removal now records new container/member revisions and publishes their removal together. Explicit source-wide purge is available through REST `DELETE /sources/{id}?purge=1`, `brain sources remove ID --purge` and the browser's **Purge calendar…** action. A purge persists its authorized intent before cleanup, stops source writes, settles interrupted snapshot writes and removes owned files in bounded journal batches. It works after ordinary removal and before any snapshot has been accepted. Completion erases the protected link and root/member payload lineage. Configured source tombstones remain removed at startup without trying to decrypt an erased link.

Purge recovery runs at startup and in the polling recovery loop. It can finish after the requesting credential is revoked; the durable intent records an already-authorized operation. Unreadable or conflicting owned files leave a sanitized pending error, and repairing the obstruction allows recovery to complete. Purge scans bypass ingestion ignore rules and reserved-directory skips, and report owned symlinks without following them. A dedicated test removed 1,100 historical snapshot files, the accepted snapshot and a hidden trash original while preserving an unrelated file. General retention of accepted history is still separate work.

Retention policy is now modeled and validated in YAML and the settings API, including reload without restart. Temporary-record cleanup expires open proposals, retains executing proposals, prunes resolved proposal metadata, removes expired API idempotency rows and old retrieval traces, and collects unowned payloads. Conversation references, direct foreign keys and active journal plans protect payloads. Removing the last known owner permits immediate collection; unattached writes receive the configured orphan grace period. Expiring a proposal also appends a retained conversation event.

The metadata worker runs hourly and drains bounded batches, with a shorter retry for backlog or transient database failures. Administrators can request a batch through `POST /v1/maintenance/retention/metadata`; session requests require recent-password confirmation and writer-side authority is checked again. This is a temporary-record endpoint, not the full document/file retention operation.

Document retention now applies the configured trash and removed-record periods. Expiry is recoverable across file finalization and index publication, and preserves unowned external originals.

Expired removed identities release their occurrence and calendar-member mappings so a later import can receive a new identity. User-deleted identities keep their suppression. Parent locking holds calendar refresh until member expiry and identity detachment finish. Changed or inaccessible owned files are deferred, attempts rotate so one conflict does not starve other records, and an already-missing file can still have its retained payloads purged.

The initial encrypted backup codec now uses a fresh AES-256 data key per archive, wrapped under a 32-byte backup key. Version `SBKB0001` carries an 84-byte header, followed by 1-MiB authenticated segments. Segment authentication binds the complete header hash, sequential index and length; a required authenticated empty frame prevents undetected truncation, and trailing bytes are rejected. Working plaintext/ciphertext buffers stay fixed at two MiB and are cleared with the data key after use. The implementation follows the [current .NET AES-GCM size constraints](https://github.com/dotnet/docs/blob/main/docs/standard/security/cross-platform-cryptography.md) and [explicit tag-size guidance](https://github.com/dotnet/docs/blob/main/docs/fundamentals/syslib-diagnostics/syslib0053.md).

[Cipher evidence](evidence/m4-backup-cipher-20261024/verification.json) records **28 focused passing checks**, including nonseekable fragmented input, header/tag/ciphertext tampering, wrong keys, omitted/reordered/duplicated/foreign frames, cancellation, truncated completion and a generated 32-MiB stream. The prior full regression remains the 2,214-test folder-purge checkpoint; these 28 checks were run separately. This is an internal encryption foundation, not a completed backup feature. Snapshot/manifest integration, atomic archive publication, rotation, restore/export, preserved key material and sustained-edit acceptance remain open. Decrypted output must stay in private staging until both full authentication and manifest verification succeed. No production archive or backup key was created or changed.

The backup snapshot foundation now captures the state database and a file-version manifest under a combined journal/publication barrier. It waits for prepared/applied file mutations to finish, avoiding the gap between filesystem replacement and the authoritative revision. File metadata lives in a temporary SQLite catalog and is enumerated in bounded pages. Corpus bytes are copied after the barrier; journal replacement, removal and recovery preserve captured bytes before changing a file. Descriptor-based reads reject links and detect changed files. Unjournaled external changes become partial manifest rows after bounded retries.

[Snapshot evidence](evidence/m4-backup-snapshot-20261024/verification.json) records **2,254 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Thirteen final focused snapshot tests include 48 real content edits, trash/purge after capture, a pause after file apply, private workspace modes, cancellation, external changes and independent data roots. Initial regression exposed a manifest-registration race across roots; registration now follows the catalog commit and hooks consult only their own data root. Initial edit-fixture mistakes were corrected to exercise actual content writes. After the full regression, a one-line data-root normalization and its added trailing-separator case passed all 13 focused snapshot checks. No browser behavior changed.

This remains an internal backup foundation. Encrypted package assembly, manifest verification, atomic publication, key-material handling, restore/export, rotation, interrupted-workspace recovery and pre-migration integration are still required. The focused snapshot test is not full encrypted-restore acceptance under sustained edits or a large-corpus latency qualification. Production remains unchanged.

Encrypted package assembly now combines the captured state and files with bounded manifest records. The inner `SBKP0001` stream records instance/epoch/schema metadata, processing generations, caller-supplied embedding descriptors, root mappings and per-file hashes/revisions; a final count/hash record is covered by the outer authenticated completion marker. An incremental encryption writer requires explicit successful completion. Atomic publication creates private files, synchronizes them and the directory, and labels incomplete file sets with `.partial.sbk`.

Restore verification first authenticates a bounded private package, then checks paths, duplicate entries, file sizes/hashes, manifest counts/hash, the state migration ledger and schema fingerprint, instance id, account epoch, database integrity and foreign keys. Only a verified private workspace is returned. Failed workspaces are removed, and partial packages remain explicitly partial. This stage does not install or modify the running state or external source roots.

[Package evidence](evidence/m4-backup-package-20261024/verification.json) records **2,279 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. The 52 focused cipher/package checks include an encrypted round trip during 32 content edits and recovery of an actual Data Protection/HMAC key ring: restored state can decrypt its protected calendar link and verify a saved signature. Filesystem checks verify private modes and failure cleanup; malformed or corrupt packages are rejected. The initial schema lookup used SQLite's unused `user_version` field; it now uses the repository's actual migration ledger plus a complete schema hash. No browser behavior changed.

The daemon operations, administrator API/CLI, backup-key provisioning, complete root/embedding-descriptor capture, restore installation/path remapping/epoch bump/index rebuild, rotation, export, interrupted-workspace recovery and pre-migration integration remain open. Restore staging currently needs space for both the authenticated package and extracted files. Full daemon restore under sustained edits and hardened deployment are still required. Production remains unchanged.

The daemon now creates encrypted archives through the administrator API, `brain maintenance backup`, and **Settings → Encrypted backups**. A private external 32-byte key is required; the key-status endpoint reports readiness without returning it. The service automatically captures registered index-mode source folders along with the vault, trash and local key ring, and reads embedding descriptors from the captured state. It checks free space, rejects simultaneous backups, rechecks administrator authority before publication and labels partial archives. Downloads use authenticated private streams, with no-cache responses and an atomic, size-checked CLI destination.

[Backup-control evidence](evidence/m4-backup-controls-20261024/verification.json) records **2,294 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Focused checks cover creation/listing/download/manifest verification, missing keys, source-root inclusion, insufficient capacity, credential revocation, CLI download failure/overwrite handling and private key-file validation. Reviewed golden changes add the backup configuration, service bindings and eight versioned/compatibility API routes. Browser qualification uses synthetic notes and keys; the downloaded archives are authenticated and manifest-verified in isolated staging.

Desktop and phone checks passed at 1280 and 390 pixels, including creation, download, configured-UTC dates and no horizontal overflow. Restore installation and path remapping, account-epoch invalidation, index rebuild, key provisioning, archive rotation, export, interrupted-workspace recovery and pre-migration integration remain open. The `keep` option is validated and reloadable but does not yet delete old archives. Restore verification still needs space for the authenticated package and extracted files. This checkpoint does not close full daemon restore under sustained edits or hardened-deployment acceptance. No production configuration, key, archive or service was changed.

Offline restore is now available through `brain maintenance restore ARCHIVE` and `brain maintenance restore --rollback`. The CLI authenticates and verifies the archive in private staging, checks capacity, maps approved external roots, and installs the state, vault, trash, key ring and external files while retaining the root lock. It remaps internal paths, advances the account epoch beyond both the source and destination, revokes old credentials, expires pending approvals and marks unfinished jobs for review. It then rebuilds the disposable index before allowing normal startup.

A durable installation record coordinates directory replacements. A failed or interrupted installation blocks startup; rollback restores every previous directory and can itself resume after interruption. Previous and prepared folders remain available for review. Configuration, provider secrets and the backup key stay outside this replacement. The CLI rejects partial archives, changed verified files, unsafe root mappings and replacement of the configured incoming root.

[Restore-installation evidence](evidence/m4-restore-installation-20261024/verification.json) records **2,312 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Eighteen focused checks cover installation, interruption recovery, startup fencing and the real CLI. Fault injection covers old-directory moves, new-directory moves, index rebuild and interrupted rollback completion. The initial edit test correctly produced proposals when using an API key; it now uses an authorized session and asserts actual committed revisions.

This completes the offline installation checkpoint, not full M4 operations acceptance. Full live-daemon restore under sustained edits, hardened deployment, large-corpus resource checks, external mount-point qualification, backup rotation, export, cleanup and pre-migration integration remain open. Directory swaps require renameable destinations with writable parents; host-side path mapping may be needed for mounted external sources. No production data or service was changed, and no new browser surface was introduced.

Backup rotation now applies `backup.keep` after creation, hourly, and through manual retention. It keeps the configured newest archives and preserves the latest complete archive if newer attempts are partial; a just-created archive is also protected for its creation response. Removal runs in bounded batches, recovers quarantined files before reevaluating policy, and leaves unknown files and linked entries untouched. Settings now exposes a numeric retention editor without changing the key or source settings.

Portable export is available at `POST /v1/maintenance/export`, `brain maintenance export --to PATH`, and **Settings → Export your data**. A single pinned snapshot produces a plaintext TAR containing 51 reviewed JSON Lines tables, original files, metadata and a checksum manifest. Authentication records, signing keys, protected calendar links, HTTP validators, provider endpoint details and the raw state database are omitted. New tables or columns require an explicit policy update. Files use safe per-export paths with their original locations recorded in the manifest. Partial source files are labelled; the CLI returns exit 4. Downloads stream through private temporary files and server staging is removed when the response closes.

All four screenshots were reviewed, with no horizontal overflow or console warnings/errors.

Final review also closed a backup/export parent-directory link gap: every root ancestor is now opened without following links, and a regression test rejects a source redirected into a private tree. Export path checks cover backslashes, reserved filenames, trailing dots, case collisions and long names. The initial export status mismatch was caught by tests that required original file bodies, then fixed before final qualification. No production service, data, secret or subscription was changed.

Key provisioning, cleanup of interrupted workspaces and debug logs, encrypted pre-migration integration, full daemon restore under sustained edits, mounted-root and large-corpus qualification, hardened deployment and remaining M4 provider/enrichment/release gates remain open. Ordinary export intentionally omits authentication state and does not replace an encrypted restore archive.

Key setup, owned temporary-file cleanup and the versioned M4 upgrade are now implemented. With the daemon stopped, `brain maintenance backup-key --recovery-copy PATH` creates a private random key and matching recovery copy, or verifies the existing pair without replacing either. It rejects unsafe parent locations and a running daemon. The recovery copy still needs to be held off the server by the operator; no production key was created.

Backup, export and restore staging now carries an ownership marker and an operating-system file lock. Startup and scheduled/manual retention remove abandoned marked workspaces in bounded batches while preserving active operations, unmarked folders and retained restore rollback directories. Timestamped owned debug-body log files expire under `retention.debug_log_days`, which is editable in Settings. This adds cleanup for that format; it does not introduce a debug-body logging producer.

An initialized pre-M4 database now requires a complete encrypted archive before its M4 schema transition. The migration records applying/applied phases and the archive name, retries after interruption, and lets the index finish after the state transition. A missing key or partial backup stops the upgrade before M4 schema changes. Fresh initialization and subsequent M4 startup need no backup key. Verified pre-M4 archives are upgraded in private restore staging; obsolete local M0 bootstrap rollback copies are removed only after both stores finish. Existing encrypted archives use ordinary backup retention.

Desktop and phone checks at 1280 and 390 pixels passed for editing the debug-log period, saving/reloading, cleanup confirmation/cancellation and manual cleanup, with no horizontal overflow. Both screenshots were reviewed. The fixture used synthetic notes and stopped successfully. There was one expected pre-login 401; stopping its host before closing the tab produced reconnect diagnostics after the workflow. Production remains unchanged. Full daemon backup/restore under sustained edits, mounted external-root and large-corpus qualification, hardened deployment, real transcript U3/U15 and live-model checks, remaining enrichment/provider/budget work and release operations are still required. The [key, cleanup and migration evidence](evidence/m4-key-cleanup-migration-20261024/verification.json) records **2,341 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. All current inference consumers now share a durable model-usage ledger: chat and its tool-loop continuations, query embeddings, document embeddings and both reranking paths. Reservations serialize with the state writer and enforce the same UTC daily and per-credential rolling-hour caps. Actual input/output/cache totals settle each call; missing, malformed or interrupted totals retain the reservation. Streaming usage is aggregated with the SDK's additive usage contract and only settles reported totals after successful completion. Credential checks happen before interactive spend; admitted ingestion retains its initiator and current processing job, including calendar members whose embedding job inherits the container import's attribution.

Legacy chat reservations and deleted-conversation charges still count, with no double-counting as new calls enter the shared ledger. Deleting a conversation preserves usage; startup settles abandoned reservations without refunding their charge. The additive usage table requires application schema version 5. Both pre-M4 and earlier-M4 upgrades use the complete encrypted-backup gate; a focused test exercises the earlier-M4 transition. Portable exports explicitly include the new ledger table.

Administrators can read GET /v1/usage (and /usage), use brain usage --json with optional --from/--to intervals up to 31 days, and view today's usage in Settings. Reports include provider/model/purpose/credential/job attribution, charge and input/output/cache totals, and an explicit 500-group truncation flag. Settings provides a numeric daily-budget editor; a zero budget pauses model calls while keyword search remains available. Dollar cost calculation and future enrichment/classification consumers are not completed by this checkpoint.

The desktop and phone workflow passed at 1280 and 390 pixels with synthetic usage: known/unknown totals, purpose labels, numeric budget changes, reload/refresh and no horizontal overflow. Both screenshots were reviewed. The final workflow had no page errors or console warnings/errors and its fixture stopped successfully. Initial verification caught a nullable SQLite aggregation materialization error, a report interval that excluded same-timestamp calls, and an invalid CLI test credential fixture; these were corrected. Expected composition/OpenAPI additions were reviewed before updating snapshots.

The [usage checkpoint evidence](evidence/m4-usage-20261024/verification.json) records **2,357 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Automatic classification is now part of file processing. The shared ING-8 rule checks user overrides, importing-client declarations, parsed frontmatter, unambiguous transcript formats and source type mappings/defaults before asking the enrich model. Only an accepted model result above the configured threshold can supply the next choice; otherwise the format default applies. Calendar containers continue through their structural membership path.

The model receives a bounded UTF-8 excerpt, no tools, a maximum response budget and a 30-second deadline. Structured JSON is requested when supported; otherwise a bounded tolerant parser accepts a valid type/confidence object. Classification uses the shared token ledger and policy-owned provider transport. Invalid, uncertain, unavailable, budget-limited and timed-out results let ingestion continue. Shutdown cancellation remains cancellable.

A classification result and its policy/context fingerprint are stored in the extraction job before publication. Interrupted work can reuse that durable result, while revision/generation, source rules and configuration changes fence late output. The winning origin and confidence are committed with the effective properties; original properties remain preserved. This adds no database schema version beyond the existing version 5.

Settings now models classification.llm and classification.min_confidence and exposes an administrator toggle and percentage threshold. Changes apply to subsequent processing without a restart; existing documents retain their type until changed or processed again. The document metadata API and viewer expose the stored confidence and identify model selection. Classification is enabled by default, matching the specification; baseline fixtures explicitly disable it where they exercise pre-existing recorded provider behavior.

The desktop/phone workflow passed at 1280 and 390 pixels for toggling classification, changing its threshold, viewing the classified article and reading the stored 95% model confidence. Four screenshots were reviewed, with no horizontal overflow or workflow console warnings/errors, and the fixture stopped successfully. A separate local Qwen/Qwen3-8B check classified a synthetic article as article, reported confidence 0.95 and settled one classification usage call through the shared ledger. It used the real extraction protocol and local provider binding, not a recorded model answer.

Expected YAML, service-composition and OpenAPI additions were reviewed. Initial checks caught a missing test-fixture import; durable-cache tests then passed across a store restart, and verify that changed source rules or disabled classification cannot publish the old model choice. No production data, configuration or service was changed. Enrichment summaries/tags/mentions/link suggestions, batch backfill and optional frontmatter write-back remain open alongside the remaining M4 provider, operational and release gates.

The [classification evidence](evidence/m4-classification-20261024/verification.json) records **2,380 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Twenty-three added checks cover the type rules, bounded provider calls, failure handling, cache recovery, publication fences, settings and API behavior. The local-model and final desktop/phone qualification each passed separately.


Document enrichment now runs as durable optional background jobs. Eligible documents receive a short summary, up to five suggested tags, bounded mentions and internal-note link suggestions. The configured enrich role receives only a bounded excerpt of the current document, its title and its own tags. A local case-insensitive lookup preserves existing tag spelling without sending other document content to the model. Suggestions stay separate from actual links, and user tag overrides win. Original file bytes and the document revision do not change.

The shared model ledger reserves and settles enrichment calls, including an explicit job identifier and initiating credential. Both read and infer are required for manual requests and for automatic work inherited from a capture credential; registered folder sources require their enrichment opt-in. Revalidation covers source settings, revision/generation, live credentials, model/privacy configuration and the worker lease. Interrupted publication reuses the saved result; obsolete leases cannot cancel newer work. Temporary provider failures and budget denial back off, and re-enabling automatic enrichment resumes eligible cancelled work.

POST /v1/documents/{id}/enrich (and its compatibility route), brain enrich, and the document action queue the same job. Settings offers a global on/off control, and the viewer shows summaries, suggested tags, mentions and searchable link suggestions. Runtime changes apply without restart. Application schema version 6 adds the disposable link-suggestion index and a job index; upgrades from version 5 require the existing complete encrypted pre-upgrade backup gate. Native batch execution and optional journaled frontmatter write-back remain open. The write-back setting is explicitly rejected until implemented; the retained batch setting does not imply native batch processing.

Desktop and phone workflows passed at 1280 and 390 pixels for Settings changes, visible suggestions, disabled/enabled triggers and a completed repeat request. All four screenshots were reviewed with no horizontal overflow. The only console error at the fixture origin was its expected unauthenticated pre-login request; no workflow warnings or errors were found. A local Qwen/Qwen3-8B run used the real extractor on a synthetic article, generated a 418-character summary, five tags, one mention and five suggested links, and settled an attributed enrichment call. Original text and revision were unchanged.

Initial checks caught a cursor-wrap error after inference access changed; the cursor now wraps within the same scan. Tests also cover stale leases, re-enable recovery, preserved user tags, revision and credential fencing, saved-result recovery, purge cleanup, bounded model requests, invalid/ambiguous output, timeouts, budgets, API scopes, settings validation, encrypted migration and CLI forwarding. Expected YAML aliases, service registration and OpenAPI additions were reviewed. A full-suite MCP discovery check initially fell back to the older supported protocol under load; its isolated rerun passed without a product change.

No production data, configuration or service was changed. This checkpoint implements individual enrichment jobs; it does not close batch/provider, write-back, full operations, release or real-export acceptance gaps.

The [enrichment evidence](evidence/m4-enrichment-20261024/verification.json) records **2,403 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Twenty-three new cases cover model processing, durable publication, authorization, migration, API/settings and CLI behavior. The local-model and desktop/phone qualifications passed separately.


Frontmatter write-back is now implemented as an administrator opt-in. Managed Markdown files receive a marked `secondbrain_enrichment` section containing the generated summary and suggested tags. Authored fields, tag overrides and body bytes are preserved; unmarked collisions with that field are refused. Other formats and external source paths are left alone. The sandbox inspects the original frontmatter, the daemon checks the exact immutable staged text and owned replacement range, and the sandbox validates the complete output before a write is prepared.

Write-back creates one revision with cause `enrichment` through the existing mutation journal. Preparation checks the current job lease, revision/generation, source settings and active write-back policy. A prepared write has durable authority and finishes through normal recovery, including after the originating credential is revoked. Turning off the setting prevents new preparation. Concurrent file replacement produces a conflict and preserves the newer file; an interrupted rename recovers without a duplicate revision. The new revision retains enrichment metadata and processing attribution. A repeat enrichment request returns the completed result without another model call or revision.

Enabling write-back also schedules previously enriched eligible files. This uses their saved results under the administrator's setting and does not require a fresh model call or a still-active original capture credential. Fresh inference continues to require its existing authority and budget checks. Settings now exposes the opt-in, and the document view reports when suggestions have been saved. Application schema version 7 separates the accepted source-file hash from the current managed-file hash. Existing accounts pass through the complete encrypted-backup gate before this change. The migration recovers prior folder-source hashes from source-admission revisions where available. No dependency change is required. Generated storage fields are hidden in the normal reading view and remain visible in the lossless view and downloads. Completed-job backfills recheck queue capacity, and capacity rejection leaves the background worker available to retry. Shallow and deep source scans retain unchanged enriched copies; changed source bytes still import, and moves preserve identity and the enriched copy. Portable exports include the source hash.


The [write-back evidence](evidence/m4-writeback-20261024/verification.json) records **2,425 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Twenty-two new cases cover frontmatter preservation and bounds, the journal, conflicts, source scans and moves, queue capacity, the encrypted upgrade and the real-extractor API path. Desktop and phone checks passed at 1280 and 390 pixels; the final fixture verified one enrichment revision and one model call, and all four screenshots were reviewed. The reading view hides the generated block while lossless text and downloads retain it. The only pre-login error was the expected unauthenticated request; no workflow console warnings or errors occurred.

Initial verification caught the expected OpenAPI addition and a browser wait that did not wait for asynchronous rendering. Final review identified and fixed a possible reimport loop after the managed file hash changed; separate persisted source hashes now prevent it. Empty frontmatter is accepted, and queue pressure is handled without stopping the enrichment worker. No production data, configuration or service was changed. Native batch processing and remaining provider, operational, release and real-export gates remain open.

The native Ollama adapter now uses OllamaSharp 5.5.0 through the shared policy-owned transport. The registry accepts explicit native bindings alongside compatible providers. Native chat supports buffering, streaming, tools and declared structured output/reasoning, with configured context/output limits. Native embeddings disable silent truncation and validate vector count, dimensions and finite values. Exact native model discovery remains read-only; DNS pins, redirect refusal and live revocation checks still apply. Responses and deadlines are bounded, and incomplete streams fail explicitly.

Embedding identity now includes the native protocol, preventing reuse of vectors from a different protocol at the same endpoint. Retained bindings can serve an existing space while configured and authorized; after a restart an unavailable old identity falls back to keyword search until reindexing.

The [native Ollama evidence](evidence/m4-ollama-native-20261024/verification.json) records **2,441 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore, warnings as errors and sixteen new adapter checks. The NuGet advisory report listed no known vulnerabilities in the restored graph at this check. A separate live synthetic enrichment used the existing Ollama 0.33.3 service and installed qwen2.5:1.5b model, preserved the original revision and settled one credential- and job-attributed usage call. No model was downloaded and production was unchanged. Native embedding contracts used controlled responses; no native embedding model was installed or live-qualified. OpenAI/Anthropic, native batch and the operational/release gates remain open.

Native Anthropic chat and enrichment now use the official C# SDK 13.3.0 inside the provider assembly. The adapter passes explicit endpoint and credential settings through the same policy-owned transport, disables SDK retries and telemetry, and strips ambient SDK headers and host metadata before sending. Native model discovery uses the matching protocol version and authentication. The adapter rejects unsafe option overrides and incomplete responses, including streams missing the terminal `message_stop`. It preserves neutral function calls, structured schemas, declared adaptive reasoning and provider citation annotations.

An explicit `prompt_caching` model capability now places an ephemeral breakpoint after the final leading system text block. The caller's content is not mutated. Input usage includes ordinary input, cache writes and cache reads, with cache hits also reported separately. Native citation annotations remain available for future integration, but verified span-level citations are not yet implemented or advertised. Batch execution and the OpenAI native adapter remain open.

The [Anthropic adapter evidence](evidence/m4-anthropic-native-20261024/verification.json) records **2,461 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Twenty new adapter checks cover text, tools, schemas, cache accounting, bounds, explicit credentials, discovery, policy revocation, cancellation, malformed responses and missing completion. A separate run passed those checks with synthetic SDK environment credentials and headers to verify their exclusion. Initial checks caught a protocol-version expectation and the expected OpenAPI caching-field addition; both were reviewed before the final run. NuGet reported no known vulnerabilities in the restored graph. These tests use controlled local responses: no live Anthropic service call, model change, production deployment or corpus change occurred.

Native OpenAI batch processing now handles automatic enrichment backfills through the pinned SDK. `kind: openai` keeps the existing native SDK chat/embedding behavior and adds an explicitly declared `batch` capability. At most sixteen automatic jobs form one active batch; manual enrichment requests stay interactive. Both paths use the same bounded document prompt and result parser. Settings exposes the batch-backfill preference.

Reservations and batch ownership commit together before upload. Upload intent, staged-file id, submission intent, remote id, collected results and item progress persist independently. A restart preserves batch-owned leases and unsettled usage reservations. Lost upload and submission responses use provider lookup rather than blind resubmission. Unconfirmed work has bounded reconciliation periods and then fails conservatively, retaining audit metadata. Collected results survive interrupted publication without another remote model call.

Every publication rechecks document revision/generation, source policy, credential authority and active configuration. Changed, purged or revoked inputs cannot publish stale results. Missing and invalid responses have explicit per-item outcomes; known usage settles once and unknown usage retains the reservation. Native HTTP input/output size, line count, line length, item count and identifier bounds are checked. Failed redirects and SDK errors remain sanitized. Lifecycle-only bindings can finish or cancel an older model's batch without admitting fresh inference.

Completed or cancelled batches delete their remote input/output files where still authorized and release local payload references for normal retention. If the provider endpoint changes or remote deletion is refused, the retained batch metadata identifies the unresolved cleanup; old remote ids are not sent to a different endpoint. Application schema version 8 adds non-content batch metadata. Upgrades from version 7 require the complete encrypted-backup gate, and portable exports include the new metadata.

The [OpenAI batch evidence](evidence/m4-openai-batch-20261024/verification.json) records **2,487 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Fourteen native HTTP contract checks and twelve storage/recovery/migration checks were added. The desktop and phone workflow passed at 1280 and 390 pixels for editing and reloading the preference, without overflow or workflow console warnings/errors. Both screenshots were reviewed and the fixture stopped. NuGet listed no known vulnerabilities in the restored graph at this check.

Initial checks caught compilation issues, the expected service/OpenAPI snapshot changes and a prior schema-version string expectation. Review also added bounded line-by-line result parsing and release of terminal payload references. No live OpenAI account was called, and production remains unchanged. Native Anthropic batches, verified span-level citations and the operational/release/remaining real-export gates are still open.

Native Anthropic batches now use the same durable enrichment workflow as OpenAI. Their requests are submitted inline through the official SDK and policy-owned transport, without a separate upload. Opaque 64-character request ids preserve the local job mapping. Declared caching, adaptive reasoning and structured schemas map to native request fields. Unsupported schema size constraints move into descriptions while the original core validator still enforces the bounds.

Collection uses the SDK's fixed, pinned results route and ignores the provider-supplied results URL. Bounded line parsing validates expected ids, duplicates, missing entries and per-item success/error/cancellation/expiration. Cache creation and read counts contribute to total input usage; missing input never becomes a false zero. Finished native batches are deleted, and repeated deletion tolerates an already-removed batch. Lifecycle-only bindings can finish existing work without admitting a fresh submission.

The pinned native contract has no batch-level client-key lookup or documented idempotency guarantee. A known batch id resumes after restart. A lost create response stays unconfirmed and is never retried blindly or matched by scanning unrelated result contents; after the existing 48-hour window it fails conservatively and keeps the charge and audit record. Inline staging itself can recover without a remote call. This limitation is explicit and is not presented as exactly-once remote submission.

The [Anthropic batch evidence](evidence/m4-anthropic-batch-20261024/verification.json) records **2,507 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, locked restore and warnings as errors. Eighteen new adapter cases and two storage recovery cases were added. All 38 Anthropic chat/batch adapter cases also passed with synthetic ambient credentials and headers present. The NuGet advisory report lists no known vulnerabilities in the unchanged dependency graph. No schema increment beyond version 8 or browser control change was needed; both native adapters use the previously checked batch preference.

The SDK documentation's generic suggestion of batch metadata was checked against the native API and pinned source and was not used. No live Anthropic account was called, and no production service, setting or corpus changed. Verified span-level citations and the operational/release/remaining real-export gates remain open.

## Remaining acceptance

M4 remains unaccepted. A supplied real VTT passes multipart import, speaker filtering and a fresh local-model answer with timestamped citations. The user explicitly waived the pricing-specific real-transcript example on 2026-10-24 because no suitable transcript is available; it is no longer an outstanding acceptance requirement. The existing real-export evidence and its other limitations remain intact. Later checkpoints below record the completed live-feed, hardened Compose, mounted-source backup/restore and controlled HTTPS checks. Systemd/production qualification, large-corpus operations, off-server production key custody, release findings, remote CI/signing and remaining real-export semantic review are still open. The earlier M3 VPN/Cloudflare waiver does not waive these M4 gates.


Native Anthropic chat now supports explicit `native_citations`. Captured passages become inline citable documents, with metadata replacing duplicate tool-result bodies. Each request counts the source bytes before reserving usage. Native document indexes map only to its captured source registry. Buffered and streamed character ranges are accepted only when they identify a unique exact quote under UTF-16 or Unicode-scalar indexing; the adapter normalizes accepted offsets to UTF-16 within the captured excerpt. Unknown indexes, unsupported types, mismatches and ambiguous matches cannot create evidence links.

Core verifies passage hashes, exact substrings, surrogate boundaries, quote hashes and byte/count limits. Model-written numeric markers are removed from native answers; only verified ranges create links. Storage repeats span validation before settling the answer. `ChatCitation.spans` adds exact quote snapshots and hashes while retaining the original full passage, revision and hash; `granularity` distinguishes span and passage citations. Revision/deletion states and purge preserve their existing lineage behavior. Application schema stays 8. The browser and CLI show exact quotes when available.

The [native citation evidence](evidence/m4-native-citations-20261024/verification.json) records **2,535 passing deterministic Debug tests across eight projects**, with locked restore and warnings as errors. Twenty-eight added cases cover source tampering, forged markers, invalid and ambiguous ranges, supplementary characters, byte limits, buffered/streamed SDK responses, tool continuation, usage reservation, persistent history, purge and CLI output. Reviewed OpenAPI/YAML changes are additive. Immutable M2 quality recordings were preserved; replay checks the explicit passage default before omitting only the new granularity field.

[Desktop and phone qualification](evidence/m4-native-citations-20261024/browser.json) passed at 1280 and 390 pixels with a controlled native provider and synthetic text. Both screenshots were inspected; the final console had no errors or warnings and the fixture stopped successfully. The first phone check exposed a collapsed conversation list beneath management links. The disclosure now scrolls as a whole, and the successful rerun selected the saved conversation through that menu. A subsequent initial-render timing issue in the qualification was resolved by waiting for navigation network idle.

No live Anthropic account, production service or private source was used for this checkpoint. It does not establish live cloud model quality or close full hardened deployment, sustained-write full-daemon restore, mounted/large-corpus, off-server key custody, signed-release/SBOM/CI or remaining real-export semantic acceptance. M4 remains active and unaccepted.


The full daemon backup/restore workflow now has a sustained-write qualification through real loopback HTTP. The disposable instance uses the normal repositories, journal, publication coordinator, background services, real persisted key ring, bounded extraction protocol and a controlled local model provider. Sixteen 128-KiB padding documents accompany a changing note and a trashed note. Two encrypted archives were created while 34 successful HTTP edits advanced the live note; 15 and nine edits completed during the respective creation requests.

Both archives authenticated and manifest-verified all 22 entries, passed SQLite integrity checks and matched document file hashes/revisions to their captured state. The final archive retained revision 23 while the live note continued beyond it. The daemon was stopped, the public offline CLI restored the archive, and the daemon restarted against the restored root. HTTP reads returned the captured text/revision, keyword search found its rebuilt projection, the old API credential was rejected, and the retained trash item was listed and restored with its original text.

[Daemon backup evidence](evidence/m4-daemon-backup-20261024/verification.json) records the successful qualification and all 226 deterministic deployment tests after the shared fixture gained restart support. The latest complete eight-project regression remains 2,535. No production change or new runtime behavior was needed. Initial qualification setup omitted the verifier's required existing private staging directory; it was prepared before the successful reruns. This is a same-user isolated Kestrel host. Full systemd/Compose isolation, mounted external roots, large-corpus limits, off-server key custody, release supply-chain work and remaining real-export semantic acceptance stay open.


Release tooling now produces CycloneDX inventories, complete file manifests, package archives, vulnerability reports and build provenance for the Server, CLI and Extractor. Pinned Syft/Grype/Cosign downloads are SHA-256 checked before use. Inventories verify the bundled .NET runtime version, probe the actual native SQLite binary where shipped, and check the editor's bundled dependency versions, licenses and file hashes. Archive creation rechecks files and hashes the bytes copied. The CLI publish target now runs the server's Web SDK publish into the same bundle; inspection had found that its previous binary-only project reference omitted the browser assets and static endpoint manifest needed by `brain serve`.

The initial npm audit found the editor's DOMPurify 3.4.15 dependency affected by five advisories, including [GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7). A lockfile override alone was insufficient: Monaco also carries a copied sanitizer. The build now redirects that exact reviewed import to DOMPurify 3.4.17, fails if the upstream import/version changes or the old module remains, and records both ordinary and vendored browser dependencies, including Marked 14.0.0. This updates the dependency without claiming that the application exercised each vulnerable library configuration.

The [supply-chain evidence](evidence/m4-supply-chain-20261024/verification.json) records **2,543 passing deterministic Release tests across eight projects**, a locked audited restore, warnings as errors, eight Python inventory/package checks and clean Actionlint validation. The eight-format parser mutation corpus passed 2,056 inputs under each of two reproducible seeds. The full sustained-edit daemon backup/restore qualification also passed in Release. Current NuGet and npm audits reported no known vulnerable packages. All three fresh self-contained release inventories initially reported zero matches. A later audit found that bundled runtime identities were not canonicalized, so that result did not establish runtime safety; the runtime-security checkpoint below supersedes it. A controlled inventory changed only DOMPurify back to 3.4.15 and was correctly rejected with the five expected advisories.

[Editor browser qualification](evidence/m4-supply-chain-20261024/browser.json) passed on desktop and phone at 1280 and 390 pixels. It covered rich editing, completions, plain-text round trips, draft protection, aliases, saved revisions and PDF/CSP checks. The served editor hash matched its regenerated manifest and the declared patched dependency. Both screenshots were inspected; the fixture stopped successfully. The two intentional CSP probes were rejected as expected.

CI now audits dependencies, runs the mutation corpus and sustained-edit backup qualification, scans published packages and container images, and performs a fresh daily advisory check. A version-tag release can proceed only after those jobs and the hardened Compose smoke gate succeed. Its checksum manifest is keylessly signed and verified against the exact workflow identity, issuer and commit before a draft release is prepared. The separate live-provider workflow now selects only its intended readiness test; its inputs cannot run private-export/browser/scale fixtures requiring other setup. [Release procedures](../../tools/release/README.md) document verification and the seven-day dependency response requirement.

A disposable local key successfully signed the actual CLI package checksum manifest, and verification rejected a modified manifest. That test deliberately used no transparency service and is not evidence of live GitHub OIDC signing. No GitHub release, remote CI run, container-image scan or production deployment was performed in this checkpoint. Those execution gates, mounted/large-corpus checks, off-server key custody and remaining real-export semantic acceptance remain open; M4 is not accepted.

The subsequent [runtime-security checkpoint](evidence/m4-runtime-security-20261024/verification.json) corrected Syft's `runtimepack.Microsoft.*` package names and NuGet purls while preserving dependency references. Rechecking the former .NET 10.0.12 inventory exposed 14 advisory IDs that the original names had missed. This is a limitation of the earlier scan, not evidence that its zero-match result was safe. The old local archives are marked superseded. New packages use SDK 10.0.111, runtime 10.0.13 and corresponding Microsoft servicing packages; the transitive Microsoft.OpenApi patch advances from 2.12.0 to 2.12.2. No packages were added or removed by this refresh.

All **2,543 deterministic Release tests across eight projects**, nine inventory Python checks and 33 deployment Python checks pass after the upgrade, with locked audited restore and warnings as errors. Canonically identified inventories for CLI, Server and Extractor scan without matches. Actual Docker images were also scanned. The server/extractor base now includes Ubuntu's patched zlib package, and the egress helper uses pinned Alpine 3.22.7. No high or critical findings remain in those image reports. Nevertheless, 74 unique package/advisory pairs remain in each server/extractor image and three in the helper, with no fix version in the scanner database. The unchanged `--fail-on low` release gate still rejects all three images; those findings have not been waived or fully triaged.

The [hardened Compose checkpoint](evidence/m4-hardened-20261024/verification.json) exercises the actual daemon, offline extractor and restricted egress helper with their shipped identities, read-only roots, dropped capabilities, memory/process limits and private key permissions. Transcript VTT/SRT import, speaker/timestamp filtering, import idempotence, recurrence/cancellation, separate calendar identities, partial coverage and malformed-input preservation pass through HTTP. Desktop and phone viewer checks pass at 1280 and 390 pixels; all four screenshots were inspected and the final browser console was clean.

Encrypted backup now also passes in that hardened deployment with read-only external source mounts. Thirty-one edits completed during one backup; offline restore authenticated the complete archive, remapped all three external roots, preserved source identity and bytes, restored the captured revision and trash, rebuilt search and rejected the former session. An independent fresh stack passed the full CI-equivalent Compose workflow, including another backup with 18 concurrent edits and the meeting checks; its containers, network and volume were removed afterward. These are isolated synthetic fixtures. Production remains M3, and large-corpus, systemd M4, source-download HTTPS integration, off-server production key custody, remote CI/signing and remaining real-export semantic gates remain open.

The same hardened stack subsequently passed [real HTTPS calendar qualification](evidence/m4-hardened-20261024/calendar-https.json) against a controlled TLS peer with normal certificate verification. Explicitly permitted downloads succeeded while local-only model readiness remained healthy; another independently reachable peer address was blocked by the egress firewall and rejected by source policy. Conditional 304 preserved document revision and content-change time; changed 200 kept the member identity. Invalid HTML preserved the accepted event and reported failure, pause refused refresh, and a successful retry cleared the failure. Offline encrypted restore preserved the protected URL, source/container identity and validators, and the restored source successfully refreshed again. The synthetic path token was absent from source responses and container logs.

The first HTTPS run exposed a qualification assertion expecting `stale` where the existing source contract correctly returns `failed`; that assertion was corrected before the successful full rerun. Test-only TLS trust and network allowances were removed afterward, and both isolated Compose projects were removed after qualification.
